skill.name: runheed-setup-node
skill.description: Add Runheed error reporting to a Node.js or TypeScript app (Express, Next.js, Fastify, Bun, serverless) so production errors reach the coding agent over MCP. Use when the user asks to "add error tracking", "set up Runheed", "report production errors", "add Sentry-style monitoring" to a JavaScript or TypeScript project.
skill.summary: Set up Runheed error reporting for a JavaScript or TypeScript server and connect an MCP client to review reported errors.
skill.author: getrunheed

security_audit.summary: Most backtick alerts are Markdown formatting, but the skill does direct a remote package install, DSN handling, and an authenticated MCP connection. It does not specify payload redaction, constrain where to trigger a test error, or limit trust in live setup instructions. No evidence of deliberate data theft or an embedded prompt injection was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: The install uses a vendor-hosted archive without an independent integrity check.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a signed release or a trusted checksum. Require package verification and explicit approval before the agent installs it. Commit the verified lockfile.

remediation.issue: The workflow asks the user to paste the project DSN and suggests storing it in a local environment file.
remediation.suggestion: Have users enter the DSN directly in their host secret store or an ignored local configuration file. Never request it in chat.

remediation.issue: The workflow omits payload review and encourages optional agent session correlation.
remediation.suggestion: Document collected fields and retention. Require redaction before sending events and explicit opt-in before attaching an agent session identifier.

remediation.issue: The skill delegates setup decisions to live pages that can change after review.
remediation.suggestion: Include reviewed, versioned setup instructions. Treat external pages as reference material and ask for approval before following any new command or credential request.

remediation.issue: The verification step does not restrict the test to a safe environment.
remediation.suggestion: Use a one-off script or a local or access-controlled staging test with synthetic data. Do not deploy a public error route.

remediation.issue: MCP setup connects the coding client to a remote service that can return production error details.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the data made available to the client. Require approval before registration and use the narrowest available project access.

content.user_title: Set Up Runheed Error Tracking for Node.js
content.value_statement: Production errors can be hard to diagnose when your coding agent cannot see them. This skill guides Runheed setup, test reporting, and MCP client connection.
actual_capabilities: Guide Runheed project creation and configuration of the project DSN.
Show how to install and initialize the Runheed SDK in an application.
Describe Express middleware, Next.js request error hooks, and Bun error callbacks.
Explain when to flush pending events in serverless functions and during server shutdown.
Verify delivery using a temporary test error and the Runheed dashboard.
Document MCP setup for Claude Code and Cursor.
limitations: A user must create a Runheed project and authenticate the MCP client.
The guide does not include a dedicated Fastify integration example.
Caught errors need explicit reporting, and workers and child processes need their own SDK initialization.
The guide does not verify package integrity or define which event fields need redaction.

use_cases.title: Instrument an Express API
use_cases.description: Initialize error reporting and place Express error middleware after the application routes.

use_cases.title: Check serverless event delivery
use_cases.description: Review where a function should flush pending errors before returning its response.

use_cases.title: Connect an incident review client
use_cases.description: Review what error details the coding client can access before connecting it to an approved Runheed project.

prompt_templates.title: List setup requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify my server framework and list the requirements for Runheed. Do not install anything or read secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Express integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the startup file and middleware order in my Express app. Show where Runheed should be initialized and ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review serverless delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my serverless error handlers for missing flush calls. Propose a staging test with synthetic data and no public test route.

prompt_templates.title: Review production rollout and MCP access
prompt_templates.prompt: Review SDK provenance, event redaction, and MCP project access for this rollout. Identify which steps require approval before package installation, deployment, or client registration.

output_examples.input: Where should Runheed be added to my Express service?
output_examples.output: Initialize the SDK in the earliest server entry point. Register the error middleware after all routes. Enter the project DSN through your host secret settings.

output_examples.input: Why did my serverless test error not appear in the dashboard?
output_examples.output: The invocation can end before the SDK sends queued events. Wait for the SDK to flush before responding. Repeat the test in staging with synthetic data.

best_practices: Enter the DSN directly in approved secret settings and keep it out of chat and version control.
Verify the SDK archive and review which error fields leave your application before deploying.
Test with synthetic data in staging and authorize only the MCP project access you need.
anti_patterns: Installing a remote archive or accepting updated setup instructions without review.
Deploying a public route that deliberately throws an error.
Reporting sensitive error messages or attaching agent session identifiers without approval.

faq.question: What do I need before setup?
faq.answer: Create a Runheed project and configure its DSN in your app environment. Enter the DSN directly rather than pasting it into a conversation.

faq.question: Can I reuse the Express setup in Next.js?
faq.answer: No. The guide uses the Next.js request error hook and advises keeping Node-only imports out of the Edge build.

faq.question: Are caught exceptions reported automatically?
faq.answer: Not if your code catches and suppresses them. Report those exceptions explicitly after checking that the payload contains no sensitive data.

faq.question: Why should a serverless function flush events before returning?
faq.answer: The SDK batches events, and the platform may pause execution as soon as the function returns. Flushing gives queued events time to reach Runheed.

faq.question: Do worker threads need separate setup?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide says worker threads and child processes each need their own SDK initialization.

faq.question: Which MCP clients have setup steps in this guide?
faq.answer: The guide documents Claude Code and Cursor. It links to Runheed connection documentation for other clients rather than giving client-specific steps.
